summary: Iteration 4 backend testing — added 15 new pytest cases covering /api/auth/providers, real+demo Google branches, Apple 503, Stripe webhook (unsigned/checkout-completed/subscription-deleted), and multilingual PDF (en-GB / ar-IQ / ur-PK / zh-CN / hi-IN). Full suite 67/67 PASSED in 80.94s — no regressions across the 52 prior tests.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now ~1147 lines (was 946 in iter3) and continues to grow — auth, lex, voice, evidence, contracts, lawfirms, stripe, webhooks, multilingual PDF, languages all in one file. Strongly recommend splitting routers (routers/auth.py, routers/webhooks.py, services/pdf.py) before the next feature lands.

/api/webhook/stripe parses raw payload with json.loads when STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET is empty (insecure-by-design fallback for dev). The endpoint is publicly reachable in this preview env, meaning anyone can flip ANY user's subscription_status by POSTing {type:'checkout.session.completed', data:{object:{client_reference_id:'<uid>'}}}. Once the secret is set in prod this is fine, but the README/runbook MUST call out that going live without STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET is a critical security hole.

/api/webhook/stripe trusts client_reference_id and customer values directly without validation. If a malformed/missing client_reference_id is sent, the update_one({'id': None}) silently no-ops with no 4xx feedback — consider responding 400 when neither identifier resolves to a user, or at least logging at WARNING level when the lookup matches zero docs.

/api/auth/providers returns google_client_id and apple_services_id verbatim. These are public values (intentionally exposed to the frontend), so this is fine — but make sure no other secrets ever land in this endpoint by accident.

/api/auth/google demo fallback path will create a brand-new user from any (email, google_id) pair the caller chooses, with trial credit. With GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID empty in prod, this becomes an unauthenticated account-creation oracle. Document that GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID MUST be set before production launch (or guard the demo branch behind a DEV_MODE flag).

/api/pdf/inline still echoes user-supplied filename verbatim into the Content-Disposition header without sanitising — same issue flagged in iter3, still unfixed. Reuse the safe_fname routine from /pdf/file/{id}.

build_pdf calls _qr_for_signup() inside the per-page _on_page callback, regenerating the QR PNG on every page render. Move QR generation outside the closure (build once per document) to avoid quadratic work on multi-page PDFs.
Apple JWKS fetch (https://appleid.apple.com/auth/keys) has no caching — every Apple sign-in attempt does a fresh HTTPS round-trip. Cache JWKS for ~1h to reduce latency and Apple-side rate-limit risk.
test_credentials: Auto-generated per run via /api/auth/signup (test_<rand>@advocate.app / Test12345!). Pre-seeded test@advocate.app / Test12345! also valid per /app/memory/test_credentials.md.
seed_data_creation: test_pdf_file_recording seeds one synthetic legal_files doc (type='recording'). test_stripe_webhook_checkout_completed_activates_user persists a stripe_customer_id ('cus_test_<rand>') on the run-time test user and then test_stripe_webhook_subscription_deleted_cancels_user reuses that id to verify the cancel branch.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All 4 new feature areas are stable: (1) /api/auth/providers returns the env-driven shape; (2) /api/auth/google demo branch (legacy email+google_id) still works AND the credential-only branch correctly drops to demo-fallback validation when GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID is empty; (3) /api/auth/apple returns 503 cleanly; (4) /api/webhook/stripe accepts unsigned payloads when STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET is empty and correctly mutates user.subscription_status both for checkout.session.completed (active) and customer.subscription.deleted (canceled, looked up by stripe_customer_id). Multilingual PDFs all return application/pdf with size > 30KB confirming Noto fonts + QR PNG embedded. If the next iteration sets GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID or APPLE_SERVICES_ID, expect test_apple_returns_503_when_not_configured and test_google_credential_only_without_client_id_returns_400 to start failing — they pin the unconfigured-state behaviour.
